items.title: Write the multi-host candidate routing execution plan
items.context: Define deterministic and host-proposed keyword inputs, local search/ranking, candidateSpecSet schema, full-read budget, escalation, evidence, quality gates, milestones, rollout, and validation matrix with an honest delivery-state boundary.

happy.desc: Inspect the execution document and verify it defines the end-to-end producer flow from deterministic CLI keywords plus semantic proposals from Codex CLI, Claude Code CLI, and Antigravity CLI through local rg search, auditable ranking, bounded candidateSpecSet, top-N full reads, structured read evidence, milestones, rollout, validation matrix, and an explicit plan-only delivery-state boundary -> every required decision is concrete enough to implement and no runtime completion is claimed; WHY: proves the document is an executable canonical plan rather than a vague recommendation

edge.desc: Review the plan against sparse matches, excessive/noisy matches, duplicate aliases, keyword disagreement across hosts, unavailable or quota-limited hosts, and zero-candidate results -> deterministic fallback, deduplication/ranking, configured bounds, host-substitution policy, and explicit escalation behavior remain defined without silently widening to the whole corpus; WHY: covers boundary conditions most likely to reintroduce omissions or unbounded token use

adversarial.desc: Attempt to satisfy the proposed contract with host-supplied keywords alone, fabricated/self-reported read claims, or an unexplained full-corpus scan -> the plan requires CLI-owned deterministic seeds and bounds, local auditable search/ranking artifacts, evidence tied to actual candidate reads, explicit full-scan reasons, and quality/token/read-evidence acceptance gates that reject those bypasses; WHY: prevents prompt-only compliance and a disguised return of the 2 MB corpus injection failure
